title: Gluing K-flat tensor comparisons along a stupid tail
statement: Let R be a commutative ring and B a commutative R-algebra. Let Q be a cochain complex of R-modules and k an integer with Q^n=0 for n<k. Set T=\sigma_{\ge k+1}Q (the stupid truncation) and S=Q^k[-k] (the one-term complex). Suppose that for each of S and T, every quasi-isomorphism g:F\to S or g:F\to T with F K-flat [def-pc-module-kflat-complex] remains a quasi-isomorphism after termwise tensoring with B. Then for every K-flat P and quasi-isomorphism f:P\to Q, the termwise tensor map f\otimes_R B is a quasi-isomorphism. No upper bound or Tor hypothesis is imposed on Q.

source.place: Section 15.60, Lemmas 15.60.7, 15.60.9, 15.60.12 and Definition 15.60.13; parent Tag 08IB final affine calculation

proof.text: Use ModuleCat.hasFunctorialFlatResolution and the source KFlat instance cochainComplex_kFlat_isLeftDerivabilityStructure to choose a K-flat resolution g:L -> B[0], and similarly a K-flat resolution a:E -> X when testing an outer vertex. These source instances are fully proved; no Sheaf resolution theorem is imported. K-flatness [def-pc-module-kflat-complex] makes a tensor L and E tensor g quasi-isomorphisms. The exchange equation (E tensor g) followed by (a tensor B[0]) equals (a tensor L) followed by (X tensor g); two-of-three identifies the quasi-isomorphism assertions for a tensor B[0] and X tensor g. The natural one-term tensor isomorphism identifies a tensor B[0] with the termwise map in each hypothesis. Apply [lem-pur-quasi-iso-cone-acyclic] and [lem-pc-tensor-mapping-cone-iso] to obtain that X tensor Cone(g) is acyclic for each outer vertex. Lean helpers tensor_exchange_quasiIso_iff, tensor_single_quasiIso_iff, and tensor_cone_acyclic_iff prove these steps completely.

The proved helper exists_stupid_tail_triangle constructs T -> Q -> S with T the stupid tail and S the one-term bottom complex. Projection to S is a chain map because every possible incoming differential has zero source. In degree k the tail vanishes and the projection is an isomorphism; in degrees above k the inclusion is an isomorphism and S vanishes; below k all three terms vanish. These give degreewise splittings. The homotopy-category triangle is distinguished by the first clause of [lem-weil-pbc-degreewise-split-derived-triangle]. Apply the triangulated total-tensor bifunctor with Cone(g), using the proved source instance HomotopyCategory tensor IsTriangulated in BifunctorTriangulated. The two outer vertices are acyclic by step 1, so [lem-pc-acyclic-triangle-two-out-of-three] makes Q tensor Cone(g) acyclic.

Use the cone and exchange equivalences from step 1, now for the specified K-flat P and quasi-isomorphism f:P -> Q. Acyclicity of Q tensor Cone(g) gives the quasi-isomorphism of f tensor B[0], and the natural one-term tensor isomorphism gives exactly the termwise tensor map in the conclusion.

proof_origin.place: Lemmas 15.60.9, 15.60.12 and Definition 15.60.13; mapping-cone realization using source K-flat and triangulated tensor APIs; fully proved source ordinary-module resolution instances, tensor exchange, tensor-cone isomorphism and triangulated total-tensor functor (Y3). No abstract derived functor or derived counit is constructed.

theorem quasiIso_tensor_of_stupid_tail
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {B : Type u} [CommRing B] [Algebra R B]
    (Q : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ) (k : ℤ)
    (hbelow : ∀ n : ℤ, n < k → IsZero (Q.X n))
    (hsingle : ∀ (P : CochainComplex.KFlat (ModuleCat.{u} R))
      (f : P.obj ⟶ (HomologicalComplex.single (ModuleCat.{u} R)
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ) k).obj (Q.X k)), QuasiIso f →
      QuasiIso ((((tensoringRight (ModuleCat.{u} R)).obj (ModuleCat.of R B)).mapHomologicalComplex
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).map f))
    (htail : ∀ (P : CochainComplex.KFlat (ModuleCat.{u} R))
      (f : P.obj ⟶ Q.stupidTrunc (ComplexShape.embeddingUpIntGE (k + 1))), QuasiIso f →
      QuasiIso ((((tensoringRight (ModuleCat.{u} R)).obj (ModuleCat.of R B)).mapHomologicalComplex
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).map f))
    (P : CochainComplex.KFlat (ModuleCat.{u} R)) (f : P.obj ⟶ Q)
    (hf : QuasiIso f) :
    QuasiIso ((((tensoringRight (ModuleCat.{u} R)).obj (ModuleCat.of R B)).mapHomologicalComplex
      (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).map f)
